learningObjective: Reason about which parts of an MLP block can be fused into a single GPU kernel and where the fusion boundary lies for a Fused-QKV/-MLP style optimization.
stem: A standard MLP block computes y = down(activation(up(x))) with intermediate size F. For x shape [B, N, D] and F > D, which fusion strategy is most consistent with how modern LLM inference kernels are structured?

options.text: Fuse up + activation into one kernel (writing intermediate a of shape [B, N, F] to HBM) and keep down as a separate GEMM. The [B, N, F] tensor is written and read once, which is acceptable because the down GEMM is a big matmul that would not fuse with an elementwise activation without hurting its tile design.

Fuse up + activation + down into a single kernel that never materializes the [B, N, F] intermediate in HBM, using a K-block reduction over the intermediate dim to stream partial outputs directly into y. Because F is a reduction dim, this fusion is a producer-consumer along a shared iteration space.

Do not fuse anything: three separate kernel launches (up GEMM, activation, down GEMM) let each op run its optimal tile shape and give the profiler cleaner boundaries; fusion of any pair uniformly slows the block due to register pressure.

Fuse up + down into a single kernel by concatenating W_up and W_down^T into one weight matrix, then apply the activation last. This yields one GEMM with concatenated weights and one final elementwise activation.

explanation: up + activation is a classic producer-consumer fusion: the activation is elementwise on the [B, N, F] intermediate a, so both share the same iteration space and combine cleanly into one kernel. down is a separate GEMM: fusing it with the elementwise activation would force down's tile design to also handle the elementwise transform, and — crucially — down accumulates over the F dimension, so it cannot avoid reading a. Skipping the a materialization to HBM would require a K-reduction fusion that changes down's tiling and is rarely a win for standard MLPs (it is used by more specialized techniques like producer-consumer fused MLP with persistent kernels). The standard, robust choice is: fuse up + activation, keep down separate.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: the mainstream production fusion boundary.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: attractive on paper but hard in practice — the K-reduction fusion changes down's tile design and rarely wins on standard MLP shapes.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: fusing up + activation is a well-known, robust win.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: cannot concatenate weights of different reduction axes into one GEMM (up reduces over D, down reduces over F).

assumptions: F > D so the intermediate [B, N, F] is larger than the input/output.
Standard elementwise activation (GELU/SiLU) that is cheap per element.
nonImplications: Does not imply that no framework fuses down; some specialized inference libraries do implement full-block fusion.
Does not imply that writing [B, N, F] to HBM is free; on very small B*N the fused up+act is memory-bound and might even benefit from further fusion.

distractorRationales.B: Overstates the feasibility of full-block MLP fusion.

performanceClaim.scope: Fusion boundary in an MLP block on modern GPUs
